name: Dagg Thai
summary: In Thai, "Dagg" means to eat in the warmest, friendliest way possible, just like inviting close friends to enjoy a meal together.
summary2: In Thai, "Dagg" means to eat in the warmest, friendliest way possible, just like inviting close friends to enjoy a meal together. Dagg Thai, in Midtown Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood, brings patrons that same easygoing, heartfelt experience. Their dishes are served with a side of warmth, just as you’d find in a Thai family kitchen.

name: The Wolfe
summary: The Wolfe is a sports bar and restaurant inspired by Tom Wolfe, the late novelist and long-time NYC resident.
summary2: The Wolfe is a sports bar and restaurant inspired by Tom Wolfe, the late novelist and long-time NYC resident, whose more well-known works include The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test, The Right Stuff, and The Bonfire of the Vanities. The Wolfe aims to provide a classy place to enjoy food, sports and events. The decor and menu include nods to Wolfe, such as a cocktail called The Bonfire, a twist on an old fashioned with mezcal, reposado and smoked agave liquor. The menu runs from dry-rubbed chicken wings to mango Thai noodle to "Everything Crusted" ahi tuna.

name: Miriam Brooklyn
summary: Miriam Brooklyn is the original location that opened in Park Slope nearly two decades ago, and remains a neighborhood favorite for all-day brunch and warm, approachable Mediterranean cooking.
summary2: Miriam Brooklyn is the original location that opened in Park Slope nearly two decades ago, and remains a neighborhood favorite for all-day brunch and warm, approachable Mediterranean cooking. The menu highlights Israeli-inspired dishes and classic comfort favorites, including burekas, shakshuka, seasonal salads, and shareable plates built for the table. The space feels homey yet lively, working equally well for dates, families, and groups. Hospitality is central to the experience, with an easygoing vibe that keeps locals coming back for both weekday meals and weekend brunch.

name: So & So's
summary: This sumptuously-appointed, dimly-lit piano-bar-meets-supper-club evokes the feeling of stumbling into a local legend’s living room during a night out in NYC—but is also an ode to Broadway.
address: Romer Hell's Kitchen, 302 W. 52nd St., Manhattan, NY 10019
summary2: This sumptuously-appointed, dimly-lit piano-bar-meets-supper-club evokes the feeling of stumbling into a local legend’s living room during a night out in NYC—but is also an ode to Broadway and the theatrical pedigree of Hell’s Kitchen. So & So’s space is anchored by an upright blue piano on a raised stage—an homage to practice rooms and rehearsal studios. Luxurious red banquettes, upholstered walls and custom lighting take cues from vintage City nightlife, and the entertainment features everyone from local acts to Broadway stars and A-list talent, with special guest pop-ups possible.

name: Danji
summary: Danji showcases authentic Korean flavors prepared with classic techniques to enhance the taste, textures and aesthetic of each dish.
summary2: Danji showcases authentic Korean flavors prepared with classic techniques to enhance the taste, textures and aesthetic of each dish. They offer small but shareable portions served in multiple courses, allowing diners to enjoy each dish hot out of the kitchen. From its decor to its music, Danji represents the owners' idea of a great place to enjoy amazing food. Danji uses meat raised with no antibiotics or growth hormones, their fish are caught wild but not overfished or endangered, they strive to use organic and local produce, and do not use chemicals, such as MSG, to enhance flavors.

The expansive layout allows for intimate balcony and banquette seating as well as festive group dining and private parties. Enjoy outdoor dining rain or shine on the covered, heated decks.

summary: Nar Restaurant serves reimagined regional Turkish cuisine, sourced to be clean, organic, and halal-certified.
summary2: Partners Andy E. Arkun, Erhan Bahceci and Zeynep Tansug brought together a team of Turkish chefs to execute their vision of reimagined regional Turkish cuisine. Nar Restaurant sources produce from the Union Square Farmers Market and proteins from Amish Country in Pennsylvania to serve clean, organic, halal-certified food. An innovative Turkish-inspired cocktail menu that uses all house made juices and syrups and Turkish ingredients headlines the bar program, which also includes an extensive selection of craft beers.

name: Langan's
summary: Whether you're enjoying a perfectly mixed cocktail, savoring delicious food, or simply soaking in the lively ambiance, Langan’s continues to be a cornerstone of the City’s vibrant nightlife scene.
summary2: Langan’s is a beloved old neighborhood favorite that recently reopened on 47th Street in Midtown Manhattan after closing in 2018. For 25 years, the original Langan’s was a legendary gathering spot, attracting a diverse and eclectic crowd, from celebrities to political figures to cultural icons like Meryl Streep, Alec Baldwin, Senator John McCain, and Johnny Rotten. Journalists, media personalities, and locals alike flocked to the bar, drawn by its warm, welcoming atmosphere and rich history. The newly reopened Langan’s honors its storied past while offering a fresh, contemporary setting. Known for its warm Irish hospitality, the bar features an open-plan, grand horseshoe wraparound bar that invites conversation and connection. With a large liquor selection and a menu of fabulous crafted cocktails, Langan’s offers both traditional and inventive drinks to satisfy every palate. The bar also boasts an upscale New American menu that elevates comfort food with refined twists.

The hearty but vegetarian-friendly menu includes a selection of three steaks frites as well as a raw bar along with a variety of iced and baked local oysters. The bar offers a list of signature and traditional cocktails along with an extensive selection of French and American wines, regional beers and ciders. French Louie is open for brunch, weekday lunch and dinner.

name: La Pecora Bianca Bryant Park
summary: La Pecora Bianca Bryant Park offers a relaxed, all-day dining experience with approachable, quality Italian food, in a stylish and comfortable setting.
summary2: La Pecora Bianca Bryant Park offers a relaxed, all-day dining experience with approachable, quality Italian food, in a stylish and comfortable setting. They take Italian food back to its roots as a local and seasonal cuisine, with a menu that centers around house-made pastas and modern takes on classic Italian fare. All of La Pecora Bianca's pastas, including their signature rigatoni vodka, gramigna, and tagliatelle bolognese, are made daily in-house. Their drinks are inspired by the tradition of aperitivo hour on the ‘Piazza,’ and feature the La Pecora Rosa organic rosé, an extensive selection of spritzes and negronis, and signature cocktails built around Italian Amari.

name: The Quimby
summary: The Quimby is named after the United States first licensed female pilot, Harriet Quimby, a pioneer in aviation, known for her style and adventurous spirit.
address: Marriott New York JFK Airport, 135-25 142nd St., Queens, NY 11436
summary2: The Quimby is a full-service restaurant and lounge located in Marriott New York JFK Airport that's open for breakfast, lunch, dinner and drinks. The Quimby is conveniently located next to one of the world's most well-known airports. Taking from those surroundings, The Quimby is named after the United State's first licensed female pilot, Harriet Quimby. Harriet was a pioneer in aviation, known for her style and adventurous spirit.

name: Tara Kitchen TriBeCa
summary: Chef Aneesa Waheed brings the flavors of North Africa to the US.
summary2: The dishes at Tara Kitchen come from founder and executive chef Aneesa Waheed, who fell in love with the country (and her future husband) when visiting Morocco years ago. She then returned home and opened her restaurant in 2012 to help bring the flavors of North Africa to the U.S. On the menu are sharing plates like a spicy chickpea bowl, marinated olives and zaalouk (eggplant blended with tomatoes and garlic), plus salads and dips. Moroccan entrees like grilled lamb kebab and mixed vegetable couscous sit alongside a selection of chicken, lamb and vegetable tagines. Waheed has also taken comfort foods like cabbage rolls, fish cakes and shepherd’s pie and given them a Moroccan twist. The restaurant is also accommodating to vegans and those with food allergies.

In addition to offering prime dry-aged porterhouse steaks, including their signature 44-ouncer, as well as other flavorful cuts of meat, the restaurant offers an array of seafood, from fresh oysters to a hefty four-pound lobster. If you can manage to squeeze in dessert, try the hot-fudge sundae or the German apple strudel. An extensive wine list is available too.

summary: The classic NYC steakhouse, in business since 1837, is where eggs Benedict and baked Alaska were said to be invented.
summary2: In business since 1837, Delmonico's revolutionized the way we eat out: these guys literally invented eggs Benedict, lobster Newberg and baked Alaska, among other now-standards, and changed the face of fine dining in early America. The financial district location looks exactly like you’d expect from an old-school steak house—deep hues, dark woods and understated opulence in which to enjoy the huge Delmonico rib-eye and the Parmesan creamed spinach.

name: Fish Cheeks
summary: Family-style Thai seafood and great cocktails in NoHo.
summary2: Fish Cheeks has a cheeky design; its awning is layered like colorful fish scales, primary colors brighten the cafeteria-like dining room and overturned baskets serve as lampshades overhead. Brothers and co-chefs Chat and Ohm Suansilphong, whose parents owned a restaurant in Thailand, prepare Thai family-style dishes at varying levels of spiciness; standouts include coconut crab curry and steamed whole fish with aromatic Thai herbs. Non-seafood items like grilled pork cheeks with jeaw sauce and potent cocktails are also exemplary.

name: Travelers Poets & Friends
summary: Travelers Poets & Friends captures the essence of the Italian coastline with its authentic offerings.
summary2: Travelers Poets & Friends captures the essence of the Italian coastline with its authentic offerings. Proprietor Emanuele Nigro, known for Osteria57 and Alice, has created a multi-faceted venue with a bakery, espresso bar, and market. The eatery offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner menus curated by Italian chef Riccardo Orfino, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and pescatarian-friendly dishes. Highlights include tuna Bolognese lasagna, grilled fishes, and eclectic pizzas. The marketplace section provides fresh and dry pasta, exotic salts, spices, and specialty drinks. Nigro's dedication to sustainable and high-quality seafood is evident, and the venue's ambiance reflects his Italian culinary philosophy.

name: Mokyo
summary: Mokyo offers an array of Asian-inspired cuisine that blend flavors from chef Kyungmin "Kay" Hyun's childhood and travels across Spain and South America.
summary2: Mokyo is a cozy nook in the East Village. The name is a playful way of saying "Thursday" in Korean ("mok" is the abbreviation "Thurs."), and Mokyo is the sister restaurant to Thursday Kitchen from chef Kyungmin "Kay" Hyun. Mokyo offers an array of Asian-inspired cuisine that blend flavors from Chef Kay’s childhood and travels across Spain and South America. Understanding the inevitable loss to her grandma and mom’s traditional dishes, Chef Kay has found a perfect balance of Asian twists and dishes from her travels to ignite nostalgic flavors yet something unfamiliar and pleasant with an Asian flair.

Stefano Callegari, a Roman chef and entrepreneur, coined the term, combining tramezzino (triangular sandwich) and pizza. The pockets have a crisp exterior and soft interior that absorbs the juices from hearty oxtail ragu and eggplant parmigiana. Eight fillings rotate daily. While the trapizzini are designed to be portable, they’re big and messy—so it’s wise to enjoy them at a copper-topped table along with some Italian wine or beer.

The interior is a version of classic, roadhouse Americana, and the kitchen serves ’cue in the many styles of the South: Thus you get Texas-style beef brisket, Carolina pulled pork, Memphis pork ribs and Georgia chicken-fried steak. But as any aficionado knows, the sides are just as important, and Virgil’s has a slew of them, including hush puppies, biscuits and gravy, and “Train Wreck Fries,” slathered in a mouthwatering mix guaranteed to infuriate your doctor: cheddar, bacon and ranch dressing.

name: Sushi of Gari 46
summary: Masatoshi “Gari” Sugio is the Japanese owner-chef of several highly regarded sushi spots known for procuring the freshest fish on the market.
summary2: Gari initially came to the United States to help a friend with the opening of a new Japanese restaurant in New York City. He worked as a sushi chef for several Japanese restaurants, and observed many of the guests eating sushi with too much soy sauce, which masked the taste of the delicate succulent fish. He decided to create his own brand where sauce was put directly onto the sushi during the preparation stage, so customers did not need to add soy sauce to truly enjoy the taste of each piece. Gari was determined that he could create a variety of sauces that would go well with sushi. Since opening his first restaurant in 1997, the main focus has been to serve sushi with the original sauces and toppings Chef Gari has created. These sauces serve to enhance the sensitive taste and flavor of each morsel of fish.

summary2: Daniel Boulud’s tribute to the original Café Boulud in Lyon, France, this version doesn’t evoke a sense of “town folk charm” like the original does, but it is quite comfortable and well appointed with murals of the French countryside, elegant place settings and even sidewalk seating. The avuncular clientele here enjoy the finely executed cuisine, and the standouts include the Hudson Valley foie gras, the braised octopus terrine and the English pea raviolini with bacon.

name: The Parliament
summary: At The Parliament, located in the landmark Benjamin Royal Sonesta New York hotel, chef Rakmin Lee brings to life his vision of a contemporary American Bistro dining menu.
address: The Benjamin Royal Sonesta New York, 557 Lexington Ave., Manhattan, NY 10022
summary2: The Parliament serves breakfast, lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, seven days a week. The restaurant is conveniently located in Manhattan's Midtown East, within walking distance to Rockefeller Center, Broadway, the United Nations and Grand Central Terminal. At The Parliament, chef Rakmin Lee brings to life his vision of a contemporary American Bistro dining menu. The menu offers signature American cuisine, concentrating on seasonal ingredients prepared with classic techniques. The Parliament is located at The Benjamin Royal Sonesta, a restored 1927 Emery Roth hotel, a New York City Landmark and a fitting complement to the restaurant’s refined style, café culture, and eclectic interior design.

name: Fandi Mata
summary: Fandi Mata delivers a new take on artisinal, global cuisine inspired by the vast Mediterranean region, featuring classics with a contemporary touch.
summary2: Fandi Mata delivers a new take on artisinal, global cuisine inspired by the vast Mediterranean region, featuring classics with a contemporary touch. With more than 15 years of experience in New York City’s fine dining scene, executive chef Chris Cortez brings a deep respect for ingredients and a passion for seasonal, ingredient-driven cuisine. Raised on a small farm in Pennsylvania and influenced by his Spanish heritage, his approach blends rustic simplicity with refined technique—food that honors its origins while embracing the creativity and rhythm of the city he calls home.

The intimate Blue Room is encircled with original Broadway relics and perfect for small groups.

name: Morandi
summary: Morandi's rustic space is a fitting setting for its sublime Italian dishes.
summary2: Restaurateur Keith McNally named his first Italian trattoria for the still-life painter Giorgio Morandi, an Italian artist from Bologna. Inspired by his images of bottles and glasses as well as his epicurean hometown, Morandi's rustic West Village space has a beautiful tiled floor, exposed brick and a crowd that's a mix of locals and Europeans. Various regions of Italy are represented on the menu, with a wide range of antipasti, pasta and secondi like agnolotti di capesante (scallops ravioli) or meatballs with pine nuts and raisins.

summary2: Philippe Chow, the iconic New York fine-dining destination known for more than two decades of tableside Peking Duck and champagne-fueled celebrations, has opened its new flagship at 10 East 52nd Street. Showcasing modern Beijing-style cuisine with theatrical flair, signature dishes include Whole Peking Duck, Chicken Satay, Sesame Walnut Prawns, Salt & Pepper Lobster and Cotton Candy Baked Alaska. The glamorous, multi-level space offers private dining for up to 300 guests and offsite catering up to 150 miles outside of NYC.

summary: The Chemistry Room is an innovative and modern take on traditional Japanese cuisine that combines tradition with unforgettable modern flair.
address: Sanctuary Hotel New York, 132 W. 47th St., Manhattan, NY 10036
summary2: The Chemistry Room is an innovative and modern take on traditional Japanese cuisine that provides a dining experience rooted in tradition, combined with unforgettable modern flair. With culinary inspirations from Japan, France and Italy, The Chemistry Room features an omakase tasting menu with the highest quality of sourced items that bring together subtle and robust flavors. For $125 per person, there's a 15-course tasting menu by executive chef Frankie Chen. Guest will enjoy an up-close and intimate dining experience where fresh seasonal ingredients are used to curate a mouth-watering and innovative omakase.

summary2: Strip House Midtown brings all the Strip House signatures to a bi-level space on 44th Street that offers lunch, dinner and private dining. Diners can relax with a classic cocktail at the bar, or delve into the full steakhouse experience. The charred cuts are paired with decadent sides, and the siren-red interior matches Old World glamour—the walls are adorned with original Studio Manassé prints of 1930s burlesque stars—with modern style and sophistication. The namesake cut isn't the only thing to marvel upon at this restaurant, which was named a top steakhouse by Zagat and awarded four stars by Forbes.

name: Coqodaq
summary: This "cathedral of fried chicken" skillfully integrates Korean and American influences, featuring dishes cooked by a world-class culinary team, alongside the largest restaurant champagne list in America.
summary2: Coqodaq is an innovative fried chicken concept from Gracious Hospitality Management, designed by Rockwell Group as "the cathedral of fried chicken." They skillfully integrate Korean and American influences, featuring dishes cooked by a world-class culinary team. From certified humane, hormone- and antibiotic-free chicken to gluten-free and anti-inflammatory rice flour batter, and clean cultured oil—every ingredient is of the highest quality and sustainably sourced. The beverage program champions champagne as the pairing of choice, with the largest restaurant champagne list in America, with Blue Chip classics, pages of verticals of vintages, and 100 sparkling wines under $100, breaking down the cost barrier of bubbly. Classic cocktails with an innovative twist, as well as premier beer and wine selections, round out the menu.

name: abcV
summary: Jean-Georges Vongerichten performs magic with vegetables.
summary2: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's abcV (“V” stands for vegetables) is a radiant outgrowth of Flatiron gems ABC Kitchen and ABC Cocina. The bathed-in-white showroom has a bar and communal standing table up front; in the rear is a dining room facing the windowed kitchen. Good knife skills are key for chefs here, and the dice is precise on yams and broccoli stems dotting beluga lentils flavored with black vinegar and sneaky heat from chili oil. Diners can substitute shaved crudité for pita to scoop up drop-dead gorgeous kabocha squash dip. The beverage menu is creative and wide-ranging.

name: Little Alley
summary: Chef Yuchun Cheung, born and raised in one of Shanghai’s little alleys in a family of chefs and restaurateurs, decided that Little Alley should recreate the Shanghainese cuisine that he grew up with.
summary2: Little Alley is translated from the Chinese word “弄堂” or “long tang”—the narrow, interconnected alleyways unique to Shanghai—a place where when one family puts a delicious dinner on the table, the aroma of its dishes fills several blocks around. Chef Yuchun Cheung, born and raised in one of Shanghai’s little alleys in a family of chefs and restaurateurs, decided that Little Alley should recreate the Shanghainese cuisine that he grew up with. Leading an entire kitchen staff of Shanghainese locals and drawing experience from his years in the kitchen of Shanghai’s famous Quanjude Restaurant, New York’s China Blue, and most importantly from his childhood home, Chef Cheung designed a menu that’s Shanghainese through and through. In addition, the space offers a nostalgic ambience and interior design resembling that of an old long tang.

Cédric (son of Jean-Georges) is both a gifted and rigorously trained chef, evidenced by lightly fried baby squid, intoxicating corn fritters, nasi goreng (fried rice with a runny egg) and noodles with lobster and basil. Don’t miss the sundae with bruléed bananas and violet-hued ube ice cream.

summary2: Aqua New York has two separate restaurants—Aqua Roma and Aqua Kyoto—each a master of its own cuisine to bring this unique lifestyle dining concept to the table. With two amazing cuisines, contemporary Japanese and Italian, served as one fabulous experience, Aqua New York offers dining on a grand scale. Order from one menu or both, wherever you are seated. The menu reads Italian from the front and Japanese from the back. Their dinners often start with a signature Japanese sushi platter to share, followed by an Italian entrée and a delicious dessert. Italian and Japanese cooking match perfectly because they both share the same culinary philosophy: using  the freshest seasonal produce and preparing theme simply to let their natural flavors shine.

summary2: Bar Primi is a casual Italian pasta shop devoted to "primi piatti," the pasta course. What began as an idea for a small space in Manhattan’s East Village has since become a downtown New York staple, housed on the Bowery for the last ten years. With this second location in the Penn District area of Chelsea, the team carries on the same tried and true methods of making fresh pasta traditionally prepared and cooked to order, using a variety of non-GMO semolina and specialty ‘00’ flours, organic eggs and family recipes.

name: Animo!
summary: Ánimo! is an authentic Mexican restaurant dedicated to honoring the rich culinary traditions of Mexico.
summary2: Ánimo! is an authentic Mexican restaurant dedicated to honoring the rich culinary traditions of Mexico. The menu features classic dishes prepared with care, using high-quality ingredients and time-honored techniques—no shortcuts, nothing pre-made, and everything crafted from scratch. From their handmade tortillas to slow-cooked moles and house-marinated pastor, every bite is rooted in bold, soulful flavor. Just as essential as the food is the spirit of Mexican hospitality. Ánimo! welcomes every guest with warmth, generosity, and attention to detail, creating a dining experience that feels both elevated and deeply personal. At Ánimo!, you're not just having a meal—you're part of something meaningful.

name: Naks
summary: Naks by Unapologetic Foods offers a gastronomic tour of the Philippines framed by the personal memories of the restaurant’s chef, Eric Valdez.
summary2: In Tagalog, the word "Naks" carries the beautiful essence of surprise and admiration, serving as the team's inspiration to craft gastronomic delights that aim to evoke these heartfelt emotions. These meals are meticulously prepared to spark joy and wonder with every flavorful bite. Naks by Unapologetic Foods offers a gastronomic tour of the Philippines framed by the personal memories of the restaurant’s chef, Eric Valdez. Chef Eric is crisscrossing Philippines and taking inspirations from locals homes and smaller towns to present a part of the cuisine that is still hidden from many around the world. There are two ways to experience Naks—a la carte or the communal Kamayan Feast—and each offers its own unique perspective.

name: Veselka
summary: Find 24-hour comfort food and Ukrainian specialties at this East Village standby.
summary2: You can hardly call yourself a New Yorker without having a favorite dish at the famous East Village Ukrainian eatery Veselka Restaurant. In business since 1954, it offers neighbors and visitors 24-hour comfort food in a diner-type atmosphere. The kids love the pierogis and potato pancakes; the adults love the borscht and sweet cheese blintzes. On the way out it’s hard to pass up the pastry counter with its pies, cupcakes, cookies and homemade muffins. The restaurant also has a seasonal outdoor café.

name: Ammos Estiatorio - Grand Central
summary: Features upscale authentic cuisine from various regions of Greece, emphasizing seafood and incorporating Mediterranean and North African influences.
summary2: Open design, light woods and weathered stones conjure the sun-drenched atmosphere of the Greek islands at Ammos, which features upscale authentic Greek cuisine from various regions of Greece, emphasizing seafood and incorporating Mediterranean and North African influences. Many of the ingredients—sea salt, dried oregano, capers and caperberries—are imported from Greece, while many of the staples like olive oil, honey and halloumi cheese are produced on a family farm in Cyprus. The wine list, featuring 200 Greek wines, is supplemented by signature cocktails and an extensive list of beers, liquors and spirits.

name: Ilili Restaurant
summary: Ilili is New York's premier contemporary Mediterranean restaurant, offering inspired Lebanese cuisine.
summary2: Since 2007, ilili has shared the cuisine and culture of Lebanon in the Flatiron District, introducing the Lebanese table to curious diners while comforting native Lebanese guests with a celebration of their homeland. Owner and executive chef Philippe Massoud expertly crafts a sophisticated blend of modern and traditional Lebanese cuisine drawing influences from the span of the ancient Silk Road trade routes. Their warm and generous hospitality drives their mission to make every guest and team member feel genuinely welcomed and fundamentally honored.

name: Antica Pesa
summary: The Willliamsburg, Brooklyn eatery is the sister restaurant of the well-known Roman dining establishment, which has been run by the same family.
summary2: Antica Pesa Brooklyn, "your home away from Rome," opened in 2012 as the first outpost of the legendary restaurant owned and operated by the Panella family since 1922 in Rome, Italy. Antica Pesa is named after the antique scales of the 17th-century customs post in Trastevere where Antica Pesa Rome stands today. Antica Pesa Brooklyn pays homage to their homeland with a focus on the traditionally innovative dishes that transport diners directly to Rome.

name: The Dram Shop Bar
summary: The Dram Shop Bar is a locally owned sports bar and restaurant in Park Slope.
summary2: The Dram Shop Bar is a locally owned sports bar and restaurant in Park Slope, Brooklyn. For over 15 years, Dram Shop has been serving classic American dishes with a Tex-Mex twist—chicken wings, the Dram burger, salads, nachos, tacos, and more—all made fresh daily, alongside a wide selection of beers, liquors and cocktails, served by a friendly and welcoming staff. Dram Shop is the perfect destination to eat and drink, watch your favorite team, play pool and have fun. They offer indoor and outdoor dining, games, vegetarian options, free delivery, and they're family friendly.

name: Nizza
summary: Nizza takes its name from the Italian word for the French region of Nice, and its menu is French-Italian fusion.
summary2: Nizza takes its name from the Italian word for the French region of Nice, and its menu leans on regional favorites from the Italian Riviera. House-made rigatoni, pizza and a few specialties highlight the options at this relaxed Theatre District institution, which also has gluten-free alternatives and an approachable wine list.

name: DubuHaus
summary: DubuHaus is a Korean restaurant centered around authentic handmade dubu (tofu), crafted fresh each morning from organic, non-GMO soybeans.
summary2: DubuHaus is a Korean restaurant centered around authentic handmade dubu (tofu), crafted fresh each morning from organic, non-GMO soybeans. Rooted in Korea's ingredient-first philosophy, the menu features a thoughtful balance of traditional and contemporary Korean dishes designed to highlight the texture, warmth, and seasonality of each ingredient. From comforting stews to fresh seasonal specialties, every dish reflects the restaurant's commitment to everyday nourishment and sincere hospitality. Dine-in reservations, walk-ins, and online ordering are all available.

summary2: GupShup is Hindi for gossip or chitchat, a fitting name for a convivial bi-level Indian restaurant. The Gramercy space is as vibrant as Indian spices, with a big mural of a tiger and a tiled checkerboard floor. The bar offers cocktails infused with saffron, tamarind, turmeric and cardamom. Try fusion dishes like pulled jackfruit tacos or a lamb kebab burger, or go with classics such as chicken tikka and saag paneer.

The menu highlights timeless French classics, from hors d’œuvres and plats principaux to desserts crafted to embody true joie de vivre, alongside a diverse selection of prime steaks, an in-house dry-aged meat program, and premium A5 Japanese wagyu. In addition to an extensive wine list and signature cocktails, La Grande Boucherie also features an inspired menu of absinthe-driven signature drinks.

Royal 35 dry ages their steaks in-house for 30-35 days using blocks of Himalayan sea salt in their custom built "dry aging box." address: Macy's Herald Square, 151 W. 34th St., 6th fl., Manhattan, NY 10001
summary2: This modern Italian trattoria and bar on Macy’s sixth floor boasts soaring ceilings and beautiful natural light, not to mention impressive views of the Empire State Building. The menu features authentic, Neapolitan pizza, al forno entrées and house-made pastas, alongside an all-Italian wine list of more than 100 selections. The restaurant's showpieces include three wood-burning ovens and the 240-foot long Carrara marble and stainless steel sculptural bar sweeping through the spacious dining room, said to be the longest bar set for dining and drinks in NYC.

summary: Victor’s, in the Theatre District, has been a redoubt for high-end Cuban food since 1963.
summary2: Victor’s, in the Theatre District, has been a redoubt for high-end Cuban food since 1963. In an airy space, the tropical theme is carried out with bright hand-painted murals, cane-backed chairs and old-time paddle fans gently waving in the rafters. The menu is more ambitious than a rice-and-beans joint, with both a classica menu of favorites like ropa vieja, skirt steak sautéed in onions, tomatoes, onions and peppers, then shredded by hand; and a nueva menu with ambitious fare like snapper, marinated in Seville oranges, and salmon, with a sugarcane glaze.

The new addition to Park Slope offers Chef Kumar’s cooking, known for blending cultures, à la carte, along with a unique cocktail program, thoughtfully curated to complement Indian flavors. Guests have the option of sitting at the sleek marble bar, the cozy booth-lined tables below oversized windows, and quiet hightop seating. Walk-ins are accepted at all three, but reservations are encouraged for the tables (available on Resy).

summary2: Bar Sprezzatura NYC is a coastal-inspired rooftop aperitivo bar and restaurant located atop the Kimpton Theta New York - Times Square hotel. Drawing inspiration from the effortless elegance of the Italian Riviera, it offers a bi-level setting with both indoor and outdoor seating, providing a vibrant atmosphere for guests to enjoy signature spritzes, unique martinis, and refined stuzzichini. Whether you’re looking for an aperitivo, pre-theater drinks, or an elegant dining experience, Bar Sprezzatura is your go-to gathering place.

summary2: Bananas, a New American restaurant from chef-owners Chris Ng (previously of Blue Ribbon and Bond St) and Kyaw Lwin (previously of Yakiniku Futago, Hasalon and Michelin-starred Shmoné), is located in the East Village. Bananas is an expression of the team’s take on Asian American food, incorporating classic Asian flavors with Western cuisine. The phrase “Bananas” has previously been used as a slur to describe Asian Americans who are ‘yellow’ presenting but culturally white due to their upbringing in America. Bananas offers a signature menu of American favorites with elements of Asian cooking.

name: La Sirene UWS
summary: Chef/owner Didier Pawlicki's menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season.

His menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season. The restaurant's focus is on French Southern homemade styles and quality ingredients (Cuisine Bourgeoise) paired with a respectable wine list and friendly, professional service.

summary2: Since 1997, Bottino has offered classic and contemporary Tuscan Italian cuisine and boutique wines—as well as house cocktails and a bar menu—steps from the vibrant West Chelsea gallery scene. From a century-old hardware store, architect Thomas Leeser fashioned a mid-century modern eatery with a beautiful garden. Lovely for a romantic dinner, an evening with family or friends, Bottino's private dining spaces make it an ideal venue for large events as well.

summary2: Located at the historic intersection of Christopher and Gay Streets, Petite Boucherie brings a touch of France to the cultured and eclectic neighborhood of the West Village. Born and raised in Georgia, Maia has been treasuring hundred-year-old recipes to share in this Georgian cuisine restaurant in New York. Since early childhood, she developed a love for specialties that have been passed down for generations like khachapuri and khinkali. At Oda House, you can always expect to savor the richest and most delectable Georgian cooking delivered by a true Georgian chef.

Leading the kitchen is Hawk Rodman, a talented chef with years of experience in Thai cuisine and training under the renowned chef Masayoshi Takayama at the three Michelin-starred Masa in NYC. Chef Hawk brings a refined fusion of Japanese techniques and Thai flavors to the menu, delivering dishes that are both innovative and comforting. Be sure to try his signature Pad Thai, a tribute to his time with Chef Masa.

summary: The Dolar Shop's philosophy is to continuously innovate, always serve fresh ingredients, and to excel in customer service to build a strong connection with their guests, and proudly showcase the Macau hot pot culture.
summary2: The Dolar Shop Hot Pot story began in the Las Vegas of the East: Macau. The name “Dolar” comes from a Chinese term embodying the people’s willingness to work hard to gather prosperity, fortune, and never turning down any opportunities. And "Shop?"... they are artisans in their workshop, and their craft is hot pot. Be prepared to indulge in the delectable house-made ingredients. Hot Pot is one of the most beloved ways of dining in Chinese culture. Influences from both the East and West in Macau led to love for home-made fish balls and slices of high-grade beef. These top notch ingredients paired with the blend of sauces makes it a unique experience. The Dolar Shop's philosophy is to continuously innovate, always serve fresh ingredients, and to excel in customer service to build a strong connection with their guests, and proudly showcase the Macau hot pot culture.

name: Mission Ceviche - Union Square
summary: Mission Ceviche, from chef Jose Luis Chavez and partner Brice Mastroluca, has become synonymous with modern Peruvian cuisine, offering a diverse array of dishes crafted from the freshest ingredients.
summary2: Mission Ceviche was born in 2015 when chef Jose Luis Chavez and partner Brice Mastroluca outfitted a modest stall within Gansevoort Market to create an homage to the flavors of Peru. The initial success at Gansevoort Market spurred the establishment of a second fast-casual spot in Canal Street Market, and building on the momentum, the partners took Mission Ceviche to new heights with the opening of its first sit-down restaurant on the Upper East Side in 2019. The restaurant found immediate critical success after launching, earning a star from Pete Wells at the New York Times and a feature in the Michelin Guide. Mission Ceviche has become synonymous with modern Peruvian cuisine, offering a diverse array of dishes crafted from the freshest ingredients.

summary2: Casa Louie—a newer addition to the Hudson Yards area (at the corner of 37th St. and Tenth Ave.)—has quickly become a neighborhood hotspot and go-to restaurant for both locals and visitors. The menu features their homemade pastas and pizzas (including gluten-free pastas and pizza), as well as some traditional Italian dishes. summary: This chic French restaurant in Midtown has a vegetable-forward menu.

Each meal starts with an “amuse-juice” (perhaps kale, pineapple and ginger), and all house-baked breads are gluten-free.

summary: Askili Orchard reimagines Georgian cuisine through a contemporary New York lens with a menu that offers lighter, elegant interpretations of classic Georgian dishes.
summary2: Askili Orchard reimagines Georgian cuisine through a contemporary New York lens. Inspired by centuries-old culinary traditions from the crossroads of Europe and Asia, the menu offers lighter, elegant interpretations of classic Georgian dishes, crafted with seasonal ingredients and made-from-scratch sauces, preserves and breads. Alongside signature favorites, they also offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, including their popular gluten-free Adjaruli Khachapuri. Curated by a diverse culinary team and complemented by an extensive wine program featuring Georgia and beyond, Askili Orchard invites guests to discover the rich flavors of Georgia in a warm, vibrant setting in Manhattan's West Village.

The vibe is eclectic nostalgia meets the new roaring '20s—the energy is high and the cocktails swing.

name: Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar
summary: Whether you are a Thai food enthusiast or someone new to the cuisine, Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar offers the vibrant tapestry of Thai cuisine.
summary2: Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar was founded in the East Village by a group of women who have the same dreams and goals. "Rynn" (รินน์) means to pour—the owners pour their memories into their dishes and glasses—and the restaurant is a place where memories come to life through the art of culinary creations and mixology. Every dish and cocktail they serve is carefully crafted using ingredients and details inspired by the memories and childhood experiences of the owners. It's a place where nostalgia blends with creativity to create a unique and unforgettable dining experience. Whether you are a Thai food enthusiast or someone new to the cuisine, Rynn offers the vibrant tapestry of Thai cuisine. The restaurant has 30 seats in the dining area plus 8 bar seats and 6 more seats for outdoor dining.

summary: Delicious and scrumptious, Sushi Sen-nin’s selection of fish and daily catch are for both the eyes and the mouth to feast on.
summary2: Delicious and scrumptious, Sushi Sen-nin’s selection of fish and daily catch are for both the eyes and the mouth to feast on. Chef Matsu, using his extensive knowledge of Japanese cuisine, prepares traditional Japanese delicacies and dishes with his own flair and ingenuity. The menu is extensive, and while the prices can make it a splurge, the straight-from-the-sea taste is well worth it.

name: Catch n' Chop
summary: Catch n' Chop, situated on the Upper East Side, is a chef-driven modern American steakhouse with a focus on sustainable, fresh seafood and raw bar.
summary2: Catch n' Chop, situated on the Upper East Side, is a chef-driven modern American steakhouse with a focus on sustainable, fresh seafood and raw bar. Catch n' Chop exudes warmth and welcomes guests with open arms. With its cozy atmosphere, friendly staff, and a menu bursting with mouthwatering dishes, it's the perfect place to unwind and savor a delightful meal. The diverse menu caters to every palate, whether you're looking for a leisurely dinner with loved ones, a quick catch-up with friends, or a solo meal at the bar. Catch n' Chop offers a relaxed setting where laughter flows as freely as the conversation. Come as you are, and leave with a satisfied heart, a full stomach, and a smile.

name: Salt + Charcoal
summary: Salt + Charcoal is Williamsburg’s one of a kind Japanese robata grill and bar.
summary2: Salt + Charcoal is Williamsburg’s one of a kind Japanese robata grill and bar. Preparation of their signature steaks start with the chef hand selecting each piece of beef at the purveyor. It is then dry-aged for 28 to 50 days before charcoal-grilling using their unique crank grill. The result is a super-tender steak with all of the umami trapped inside. Salt + Charcoal also has a wide selection of seafood, a raw bar, and Japanese-inspired appetizers. The full bar features original cocktails crafted by award-winning mixologists, a variety of Japanese spirits, and wines specially crafted to pair with the food offerings.

Ma•dé draws inspiration from the sandy beaches of Bali for both its menu and décor. At Ma•dé, Cédric serves a menu of fresh seafood and vegetable-centric dishes that emphasize global flavors and ingredients from diverse corners of the world, while the cocktail-driven beverage program boasts everything from vegetal and floral notes, to twists of savory umami that add a distinctive touch to each tipple.

name: Paris Bar
summary: Paris Bar is an iconic French brasserie near Carnegie Hall and Central Park that serves traditional French fare from breakfast through supper every day, with brunch available on weekends, plus a rooftop bar.
summary2: Paris Bar is an iconic French brasserie nestled within the Le Meridien hotel near Carnegie Hall and Central Park. They serve traditional French fare from breakfast through supper every day, with brunch available on weekends. Known for its lively ambiance, warm service, and soulful cuisine, the menu features fresh seafood and shellfish as well as signature French dishes such as Beef Bourguignon and bouillabaisse. For those seeking a breathtaking view to accompany their meal, there's Le Jardin Rooftop Bar, offering stunning views of Central Park. It's the perfect spot to unwind with a drink, enjoy a light bite, and take in the cityscape.

summary2: David Burke Tavern is a modern American restaurant situated in a stately townhouse on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The casual tavern atmosphere of the first floor gives way to sophisticatedly relaxed, clubby rooms on the second. It offers lunch, dinner and brunch, as well as a daily happy hour. The menu features the contemporary American cuisine of which chef/owner David Burke is a much-celebrated pioneer, often accented with his signature playful approach to cooking, with a nod to elevated New York classics, paired with a curated wine list, craft beers and a specialty cocktail program.

summary: This seasonal Indian restaurant in the Flatiron District celebrates the intersection of chef Chetan Shetty’s Indian heritage and New York’s culinary vibrancy.
summary2: Passerine is a seasonal Indian restaurant in the Flatiron District led by acclaimed chef Chetan Shetty alongside owners Maneesh K. Goyal and Alvina Patel Buxani. The restaurant celebrates the intersection of Chef Shetty’s Indian heritage and New York’s culinary vibrancy, blending traditional Indian techniques with seasonal ingredients sourced from the Union Square Greenmarket and spice blends crafted by Chef Shetty’s mother in Pune. Guests can savor Chef Shetty’s inventive menu in the intimate Drawing Room, the elegant bar, and the vibrant main dining room. There is also a private dining room located downstairs who can host up to 28 guests. Walk-ins are welcome and reservations are available.

name: Rossini's
summary: Located in charming Murray Hill, Rossini's has been serving fine Northern Italian cuisine since 1978.
summary2: Located in charming Murray Hill, Rossini's has been serving fine Northern Italian cuisine since 1978. The genuine friendliness and warm service make diners feel right at home in this family-owned restaurant. Select from a wide variety of pasta, veal or fish entrees that reflect their Northern Italian roots, as well as selections from throughout other regions of Italy. Music is an important part of the dining experience: Rossini's features a pianist nightly from Sunday to Friday, and Saturday evenings they present the "Trio Romantico," which performs light opera and Broadway favorites—requests are always accepted.

name: ilili - Midtown
summary: The team at ilili invites guests to experience the heart of Lebanese, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern hospitality, right in the vibrant Midtown East neighborhood of Manhattan.
summary2: The team at ilili invites guests to experience the heart of Lebanese, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern hospitality, right in the vibrant Midtown East neighborhood of Manhattan. Whether you’re there for a memorable meal or or hosting a private event, ilili Midtown is a celebration of heritage, innovation, and the unforgettable tastes of Lebanon and the Mediterranean. ilili is an extension of three generations of Massoud family stories. These stories are enriched in joy, loss, struggle, resilience and 100 years of outstanding hospitality, making their establishment historic while creating new beginnings. Chef Philippe Massoud’s concept was simple: to revive and bring this ancient cuisine to a public who hadn’t properly experienced it.

name: Manuela
summary: Manuela is a welcoming neighborhood restaurant and bar in SoHo where great contemporary art and food combine to create a convivial atmosphere and sense of abundance.
summary2: Located on the corner of Wooster and Prince Street in SoHo—New York’s historic cast iron district—Manuela is a welcoming neighborhood restaurant and bar where great contemporary art and food combine to create a convivial atmosphere and sense of abundance. The restaurant is named for Manuela Wirth, who co-founded Artfarm with her husband Iwan Wirth, and like its sister restaurant in the Downtown Arts District of Los Angeles, Manuela in SoHo takes its cues from its namesake’s legendary hospitality, culinary talents, and famous warmth as a hostess whose passion for freshly prepared cuisine, local culture, and community are complemented by the guiding conviction that art and life are indivisible. Manuela hews to the belief that great food and delicious, nourishing meals are not luxuries but essentials to be generously shared.

name: Sweet Catch
summary: Sweet Catch is an ode to the connection between African-American people and their rich history of seafood culinary mastery.
summary2: From the low country of Charleston, South Carolina to the clear blue waters of the Chesapeake Bay, down through the muddy swamps and rushing rivers of the Louisiana Bayou, African-Americans boast a rich history of seafood culinary mastery, a connection to the land, and a respect for the fruits of the sea. Sweet Catch is an ode to this connection—a love letter to African-American culture, African-American people, and African-American love; a place of remembrance for what history has erased and a celebration of their spirit.

summary: Born from Italian tradition and heritage, executive Chef Phillip Basone's menu takes seasonal and local ingredients and places them center stage.
summary2: Directly translated as "Always Today," Sempre Oggi focuses on embracing the very best of right now. Born from Italian tradition and heritage, executive Chef Phillip Basone's menu takes seasonal and local ingredients and places them center stage. Brought forth by Robert Guarino in partnership with Simon Oren of Chef Driven Hospitality, Sempre Oggi draws inspiration from renowned Italian architect and designer, Gio Ponti. The bar's handmade ceramic tiles mimic Ponti's worldwide collaboration with Ceramica D'Agostino. A custom floating chandelier nods to Ponti's love for playing with geometric forms, light and color; at once both modern and traditional.

All of La Pecora Bianca's pastas, including their signature rigatoni vodka, gramigna, and tagliatelle bolognese, are made daily in-house. Their drinks are inspired by the tradition of aperitivo hour on the ‘Piazza,’ and feature the La Pecora Rosa organic rosé, an extensive selection of spritzes and negronis, and signature cocktails built around Italian Amari.

Hawksmoor's home, near Gramercy Park in the historic United Charities Building—which was closed from public view for over a century—boasts a 26-foot vaulted ceiling, a 35-seat bar, and two private dining spaces.

name: Narkara
summary: At Narkara, dining is a cultural journey inspired by the culinary traditions of Northern and Northeastern Thailand.
summary2: At Narkara, dining is a cultural journey inspired by the culinary traditions of Northern and Northeastern Thailand. These regions offer a deeper, lesser-seen expression of Thai cuisine shaped by distinct landscapes and ways of living. In the North, cooler, mountainous terrain gives rise to aromatic, herb-driven dishes, while Northeastern Thai, or Isan cuisine, reflects a hotter, drier climate and a close relationship with the Mekong River, favoring bold, savory and fermented flavors over sweetness or richness. Ingredients such as herbs, chilies, dried spices, sticky rice and preserved elements form the foundation of the cooking. Crafted in-house with care, the menu honors generations of culinary wisdom while embracing thoughtful innovation. Custom bamboo installations, woven pieces, and handcrafted ceramics reflect Thailand’s artistry, allowing Narkara to share the unseen taste of Thailand with New York through food, design and hospitality.

name: Psaraki
summary: Psaraki, the creation of longtime hospitality veteran James Paloumbis, evokes the charm of seaside tavernas found along the shores of Greece.
summary2: Psaraki, meaning “little fish” in Greek, is the creation of longtime hospitality veteran James Paloumbis. The restaurant evokes the charm of seaside tavernas found along the shores of Greece. It offers spectacular views of the Brooklyn Bridge, the Manhattan skyline, and the Williamsburg Bridge, juxtaposing the tranquility of its serene ambiance with the vibrant energy of nearby Manhattan. Psaraki is a place to unwind, enjoy a perfect cocktail, and savor traditional homemade Greek dishes meant for sharing while escaping NYC's hustle and bustle. Psaraki’s menu is inspired by James’ culinary philosophy, which he terms “homemade,” where each dish is a testament to the authenticity and connection of family recipes, traditionally prepared and presented as if one was a visitor in James’ seaside home. Guests can enjoy a sampling of classic Greek dishes and a selection of Greek island favorites.

Named for founder Carlos Suarez's mother, Rosemary's celebrates the warmth and flavors of her Italian home in Lucca.

The owners felt that serving thicker cuts of meat would convey their delicious taste better, so they offered what at the time were unusually thick cuts. A meal starts with "namuru" and "kimchi" Korean-style steamed and pickeled vegetables, continuing with tongue, ribs and/or outside skirt, and finishes with cold noodles or a "pibimpab" Korean-style mixed rice bowl. Toraji is committed to providing guests withan authentic yakiniku experience.

summary2: At Williamsburg's modern, chic Meadowsweet, executive chef Polo Dobkin has a deft touch with seasonal ingredients, crafting dishes with a Mediterranean bent. Crispy artichokes, house-made pastas and octopus with piquillo peppers and chorizo are among the highlights. Rolls hot from the oven are dusted with sea salt, luscious when spread with thyme-honey butter. Dobkin's wife, Stephanie Lempert, has devised some refreshing cocktails that are garnished with fresh herbs harvested from the loft garden overhead. That garden, plus patterned tiled floors, comfortable caramel banquettes and bare wood tables, makes it a pretty place to gather.

summary2: San Carlo Osteria Piemonte is like a corner of Turin in Soho. The restaurant, with its minimalist and elegant design, serves dishes that are well-crafted, beautifully presented Piedmont specialties that are reproduced with passion and flair. Evenings can start with a vermouth-based cocktail, just like in an old Torinese cafe, and continue with a Fassona chopped beef, then tajarin pasta with truffle or homemade agnolotti pockets with roast sauce. The kitchen is from Piedmont and so wine is abundant, and not just Nebbiolotry—try the peppery rhythm of a good Pelaverga.

The Atrium and the Cellar bar can be rented for private events. It's an ideal location for corporate events, baby showers, engagement celebrations or weddings.

summary2: La Tête d’Or is a New York steakhouse bringing together the essence of American tradition with a refined French flair. The first steakhouse of renowned chef Daniel Boulud, it features a richly enticing menu that offers all the indulgence of steakhouse favorites, elevated by the most premium cuts of meat and seafood offerings, plus the chef's specialty: perfectly flavorful sauces.  Designed by David Rockwell, the restaurant's grand yet welcoming decor features soaring ceilings, deep blue banquettes, and warm wood and copper accents. This thoughtfully crafted ambiance provides a perfect backdrop for celebrating timeless elegance and chef Boulud's culinary artistry.

With more than 10 years of experience in hospitality, aspiring restauranteurs Kevin Cardenas and Ruben Cabrera launched themselves with their first venture, Ceviche Fussion, which was an overwhelming success. An opportunity arose that bore this intimate and inviting venue, Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar, inspired by the Japanese bonsai tree (a miniature tree cultivated to resemble nature in a modest space and nurtured with artistic interaction). Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar is the ultimate representation of its namesake. Their cuisine is inspired by international tapas, putting an updated spin on classic dishes and bringing creative new ones, so every patron will feel welcomed and find something of their taste.

name: Becco
summary: Lidia Bastianich and her son, Joe, opened Becco in 1993, and since then it has been providing New York diners with outstanding service.
summary2: The name Becco is derived from the Italian verb, beccare, which means "to peck, nibble or savor something in a discriminating way." Lidia Bastianich and her son, Joe, opened Becco in 1993, and since then it has been providing New York diners with outstanding service. Located on New York's famed Restaurant Row in the Theatre District, Becco is open seven days a week for lunch and dinner. Becco is most famous for its innovative pasta tasting menu and extensive wine list, featuring more than 100 bottles of wine, all priced at $40.

The cocktail menu matches the space in its mix of classics (martinis, old-fashioneds) and modern drinks, like Ophelia’s Ascension, which blends mezcal, Sri Lankan palm sugar, bitters and cedar smoke. Even a simple highball feels extra special in the space, whether enjoyed at the 24-foot pewter bar or on the outdoor terrace with 360-degree city views.

Commence with pull-apart olive bread and spellbinding gruyère fritters followed by mafaldine with rock shrimp and chorizo. The hearth-driven menu threads the needle through the south of France and Italy, highlighting dishes such as cast iron sfincione (Sicilian pizza), wood-kissed escargot, and dry-aged côte de bôeuf. With a focus on Island and Coastal wines and masterfully crafted classic cocktails, bar seats are available nightly for walk-in guests. Or stop by in the morning for fresh pastries, breads and espresso.

summary2: Moono is the second project by chef Hoyoung Kim, building upon the success of his renowned Michelin 1-starred Jua. Taking its name from the Korean word for “gateway,” Moono symbolizes a literal “door” to another world and represents a passage to diverse cultures. Housed in a stunning three-story building that is a recognized landmark of New York, Moono's mission is to serve as the ultimate gateway, introducing the vibrant and evolving Korean food culture to New York City, captivating the palates of the new generation.

summary: Hidden inside Walker Hotel is Society Cafe, a market-to-table American restaurant by chef Nicholas McCann.
address: Walker Hotel Greenwich Village, 52 W. 13th St., Manhattan, NY 10011
summary2: With more 20 years of experience in the kitchen, Nicholas McCann, now executive chef of Society Cafe, has always been passionate about food. Drawing inspiration from his family recipes, Nicholas quickly fell in love with the culinary world at a young age and began his career at The French Culinary Institute in NYC. Since then, he has worked with some of the City’s most acclaimed chefs and restaurants, including working alongside chef Luis Bollo of Salinas before moving on to become an executive chef at Tessa, The Milling Room, and Corkbuzz. At Society Cafe, chef Nicholas flexes his creativity by bringing a fresh perspective to the restaurant’s ‘market-to-table’ concept. With a rotating seasonal menu reflective of the City’s local farmers and markets, guests can expect to experience chef Nicholas’ unique culinary creations alongside its intimate and classic art deco inspired space.

name: Clara
summary: Set inside the iconic New-York Historical Society building across from Central Park, Clara offers upscale New York classics.
address: The New-York Historical, 170 Central Park West (entry at 2 W. 77th St.), Manhattan, NY 10024
summary2: Clara, at The New York Historical, is helmed by longtime collaborators: Food Network star Alex Guarnaschelli and chef Michael Jenkins in partnership with Great Performances. The menu prioritizes local greenmarket and Katchkie Farm produce for its seasonal American menu. Clara's thoughtfully curated menu features fresh salads, homemade pastas, and a classic cheeseburger. Be sure to save room for dessert with the surprise cake of the day. Clara honors the work of Clara Driscoll (1861–1944), head of Tiffany Studios’ women’s glass-cutting department. For years, Driscoll and her team of "Tiffany Girls" worked in anonymity, until The New York Historical's research uncovered her role as the designer behind many of the firm’s most celebrated glass shades. Today, several of her creations are on display in the Museum’s Gallery of Tiffany Lamps.

name: Gui Steakhouse
summary: Gui Steakhouse is elevated steakhouse experience that integrates the unique flavors and techniques of Korean beef grilling.
summary2: The team behind Gui Steakhouse wanted to create an elevated steakhouse experience by integrating the unique flavors and techniques of Korean beef grilling. Unlike traditional steak preparation, the Korean method highlights diverse charms and tastes, which they've modernized to bring a distinctive twist to the classic steakhouse concept. This Times Square restaurant takes pride in the quality of their premium steaks, which stems from two main partnerships that ensure they always have access to exceptional beef. These partnerships are carefully selected based on their commitment to sustainable farming methods and superior animal husbandry: Creekstone Farms is committed to excellence, combining superior Black Angus and Duroc genetics, top-tier livestock management, and advanced processing; and Pat LaFrieda Meat Purveyors has delivered butchery excellence for 100 years, sourcing premium meats from small domestic farms, offering all-natural, organic, and grass-fed options.

name: Pulperia Latin Mediterranean Kitchen
summary: Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen serves the flavors of Latin America with Mediterranean touches by executive chef Miguel Molina, who prides himself on his creativity for reimagining dishes.
summary2: As Restaurant Row has long been a culinary destination offering flavors from around the globe, Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen serves the flavors of Latin America with Mediterranean touches by executive chef Miguel Molina, who prides himself on his creativity for reimagining dishes. At Pulperia, he focuses on fresh, simple, clean, healthy ingredients. The menu offers small plates, paellas, and unique larger fare designed for sharing, plus an extensive cocktail list, all served with the warm hospitality and fun that the Latin culture brings to dining. Leading the team is seasoned restaurateur Orhan Cakir, known for his acclaimed Argentinian steakhouses Palermo Argentinian Steakhouse & Bistro, Palermo Argentinian Bistro Gramercy, and Pierre Loti Wine Bar. Karla Medina, director of operations, brings deep industry knowledge from her experience managing the original La Pulpería location. Now, the beloved concept is reborn as Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen, refreshed and reimagined for a new era.

summary2: Le Pavillon is a culinary oasis in Midtown East by chef Daniel Boulud. Evoking a “pavillon”, a festive gathering dining space surrounded by nature, Le Pavillon expresses chef Boulud’s roots in New York City with a fresh and unique approach to fine dining in a dramatic setting. With a focus on seasonality and locally sourced ingredients from both land and sea (“terre et mer"), chef Boulud’s celebrated French cuisine, rooted in tradition with a contemporary New York spirit, is at the forefront of the seafood and vegetable-focused menu. Situated in Manhattan’s state-of-the-art-skyscraper One Vanderbilt, Le Pavillon offers a unique setting, both relaxed and inviting with a refined elegance. Designed by Isay Weinfeld, the space boasts a natural landscape composed of lush gardens and tall olive trees living among the tailored dining room and soaring ceilings, evoking a deep sense of natural splendor and genuine serenity.

Olvera, who has the critically acclaimed restaurant Pujol in Mexico City plus a few others in Mexico, sources the best chilies, heirloom beans and corn from his native country and looks to local purveyors for meat, fish and seasonal produce. summary2: Known for its wildly creative, premium American Wagyu burgers, Kings of Kobe takes everything up a notch with bold flavors, indulgent ingredients, and a touch of irreverence. But the story doesn’t stop at the bun: their American Wagyu steaks bring the same swagger, seared hot and paired with house-made sauces that hit hard. For those looking for the ultimate indulgence, they offer a selection of Japanese A5 Wagyu—rich, rare, and priced like nowhere else in NYC. Kings of Kobe is open seven days a week for lunch and dinner, with a daily Happy Hour, and an all-day bar dining menu, to deliver steakhouse-level firepower in a space that’s more fun than formal. Guests rave about the energy, friendly service, and inventive starters like giant mozzarella sticks, Wagyu “cinnamon buns,” and other sleeper hits that go way beyond beef. Whether you’re diving into cocktails at the bar or going all-in on Wagyu, the portions are big, the vibe is bigger, and the flavor is loud, proud, and unapologetically Wagyu.

summary2: Pete's Tavern, the oldest continuously operating bar and restaurant in New York City, opened its doors in 1864 and remained open as a speakeasy throughout prohibition. summary2: Limusina is a new Mexican restaurant by Quality Branded, inspired by New York City in the 1970s and ‘80s. In that era, nothing was more luxurious than a limousine. The restaurant space was once a taxi and limo depot, a parking garage where drivers would take their cars off-duty to be serviced, grab a bodega coffee and snacks, and loosen their ties before heading back uptown to pick up their clients. The restaurant mirrors that juxtaposition of glam and grit. Limusina has luxe, rich materials and custom fixtures next to raw, exposed concrete columns. Custom light fixtures are affixed to industrial, unfinished ceilings. The restaurant reflects the neighborhood it's in, on the cusp of the shiny, new Hudson Yards and the gritty lower Midtown. Menu favorites include fresh aguachile, queso fundido, long-bone short rib quesabirria, and churritos for dessert.

Another must-have is a pita pocket sandwich of kofta (meatballs) and cauliflower dripping with tahini.

Jazba's menu is inspired by the soul and diversity of these eateries’ strong connection to the roots that run deep across the country, bringing India’s beloved everyday dining culture to the East Village.

Nightly blackboard specials further highlight seasonal creativity. Complementing the cuisine is an extensive wine list featuring acclaimed global regions, alongside premium spirits such as rare single malts, small-batch bourbons, artisanal mezcals, and vintage-dated rums.

Try starters like Tuna Won-Tacos (ahi tuna, mango pico, avocado-lime crema) or Lava Shrimp (with creamy spicy volcano sauce). Each visit takes you on a trip to a destination in Asia. Traveler includes New York's first tea liquor machine—grab a shot glass, insert the coin, and enjoy. Modeled after the saké vending machines in Japanese train stations, this machine echoes the train station-inspired interior design of Traveler and features a selection of tea-infused liquors, Taiwanese bubble tea shop-inspired liqueur, and the famous kinmen kaoliang.

The only way to achieve that is to recreate them from scratch with regionally authentic spices and the freshest ingredients. Take an adventuruous journey through their menu, which ranges from local favorites, street foods, different curries, spicy and sour broths, satays, noodles, bread (roti), and rice dishes.

From classic oysters to innovative crudos and a take on the Fish-O-Fillet, every bite highlights sustainable, responsibly sourced seafood. Paired with handcrafted cocktails and curated wines, the space invites guests to experience the best of the ocean and the City.

Led by chef Oscar Lorenzzi (formerly of Contento) and hospitality partner Jonathan Charnay (formerly of Masa), the restaurant brings decades of experience to a lively, shareable dining experience in Manhattan's West Village. Lorenzzi’s cooking is unpretentious yet full of character, rooted in his Peruvian heritage and shaped by New York energy, while Charnay’s refined beverage program offers thoughtful, globally-inspired pairings. The result is a warm, soulful gathering place where South American heritage meets New York style.

summary2: Sadie's serves New American comfort classics in their two-level, full-service dining room in the historic Seaport. The kitchen takes an unfussy approach to comfort food—the kind of menu that works equally well for a leisurely weekend brunch or a proper sit-down dinner. Expect familiar favorites executed with real intention: smashed burgers, beer-battered fish and chips, hush puppies with maple butter, and desserts that feel like classics worth revisiting. Sadie's Garden Bar is their open-air social hub. Built for spontaneity, all seating is on a first-come, first-served basis. Just show up, find your spot, and let an afternoon become an evening. The drinks are refreshing and endlessly repeatable: sun-soaked spritzes, crowd-pleasing cocktails, and zero-proof options designed for unhurried rounds with friends. summary2: Leon’s is a neighborhood Italian restaurant with French and Egyptian accents from Natalie Johnson and Nick Anderer (also of Anton’s in the West Village). The restaurant is inspired by Natalie’s heritage (named after her great grandfather, Leon Hakim) and the couple's travels together across the Mediterranean. Leon’s spotlights Anderer’s deep passion for Italian cuisine, as well as his thoughtful interpretations of treasured Hakim family recipes and culinary traditions passed down by way of Egypt and France. The restaurant’s beverage program, helmed by Johnson, complements and enhances the culinary offerings, highlighting winemakers, brewers, and distillers the couple and their team admire. The restaurant’s lovely, transporting design evokes the quiet, weathered beauty of an Italian seaside town, celebrates natural light, and preserves key architectural details of the building (circa 1895), and the duo spent years hand-selecting the furniture, fixtures, and art that adorn the space.

This restaurant marks the return of that 1980s-era nameplate. Executive chef Cesar Dutan infuses elements of Italian, French and Asian flavors into his culinary artwork. He has graced the kitchens of many legendary dining rooms, including; Jean George, Amacord, Osteria Stella, Bobby Vans, Felice, Blue Bird London and Delmonico’s Steakhouse. Cesar’s passion for pastas, risottos and Italian classics, paired with his adventurous and positive spirit and approach to cooking, translate into an inspiring menu of authentic Venetian staples and flavors from across Italy with daring twists and visual flair.

name: Malvan
summary: This Carroll Gardens restaurant is named after Malvan, a coastal village in Maharashtra, western India, whose seafood–forward, coconut-rich cuisine has rarely been represented outside its home region.
summary2: Malvan is a coastal village in Maharashtra, western India, whose cuisine has rarely been represented outside its home region. For chef Eric McCarthy, Malvan offered a way to introduce New York to a distinct Indian coastal tradition rooted in everyday village cooking. This is New York’s first restaurant dedicated to Malvani cuisine and McCarthy's second coastal Indian concept, following Indian Table in Cobble Hill, a Goan restaurant shaped by Portuguese influences. A native of Goa, Chef Eric encountered Malvani food while traveling along India’s western coast. Life in Malvan is shaped by the sea and by community. Days begin at the fish markets, kitchens remain open and airy, and meals are cooked slowly and meant to be shared. The cuisine reflects this rhythm, fresh seafood–forward, coconut-rich, and grounded in everyday cooking rather than ceremony or excess.

Although the restaurant in NYC is a contemporary recreation of the one in Busan, the traditional roots on which Yoon Haeundae Galbi are built remain intact. summary: Yakiniku Gen offers a truly authentic Japanese BBQ dining experience with more than 70 branches in Japan and five in NYC.
summary2: Yakiniku Gen offers a truly authentic Japanese BBQ dining experience. With more than 70 branches in Japan and five in NYC, they proudly maintain their quality and bring the rich flavors and traditions of Yakiniku. Indulge in perfectly grilled meats, fresh seasonal vegetables and an excellent selection of saké and specialty drinks, all in a warm, inviting atmosphere.

name: Kimmi
summary: TLK-Tigerlily Kitchen is back with an exciting new chapter: Kimmi, a new dine-in concept on Canal Street in Chinatown, where Asian fusion flavors meet a beautifully designed atmosphere.
summary2: TLK-Tigerlily Kitchen is back with an exciting new chapter. Their next evolution is Kimmi, a new dine-in concept on Canal Street in Chinatown, where Asian fusion flavors meet a beautifully designed atmosphere. From innovative dishes to handcrafted cocktails, every detail is thoughtfully curated to create an unforgettable dining experience. This woman- and minority-owned restaurant serves pan-Asian dishes that, in many cases, are vegan and gluten-free. Menu highlights include Peanut Street noodles, arancini “rice balls” with yuzu and chili vinaigrette, green garden vermicelli, and braised five spice short rib.

name: Florentin Bistro
summary: This chic Neo-American bistro and bar on the Upper West Side serves seasonal, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine with influences from French, Italian, Greek, Israeli and Middle Eastern cooking.
summary2: Florentin is a chic Neo-American bistro and bar on Manhattan's Upper West Side that serves seasonal, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine with influences from French, Italian, Greek, Israeli and Middle Eastern cooking. Rooted in warm hospitality and neighborhood charm, Florentin offers an elevated yet approachable dining experience centered around fresh, seasonal ingredients, vibrant flavors, fine wine and great company. More than a restaurant, Florentin is a gathering place. Come for the food, stay for the vibe, and leave feeling like part of the community.

name: Miru
summary: Perched atop Pier 57 in Chelsea, Miru is a rooftop Japanese listening lounge, rooftop bar and dining destination that offers a tranquil escape by day and a sultry, immersive atmosphere by night.
address: Pier 57 at Hudson River Park, 25 Eleventh Ave., New York, NY 10011
summary2: Perched atop Pier 57 in Chelsea, Miru is a rooftop Japanese listening lounge, rooftop bar and dining destination that offers a tranquil escape by day and a sultry, immersive atmosphere by night. Curated vinyl soundscapes set the tone amidst uninterrupted views of the Hudson River and the Manhattan skyline, while the food, cocktails and saké transport you. With its seamless flow onto the Pier 57 rooftop park lawn, Miru’s design emphasizes intimacy and discovery. Plush seating, mood lighting and a carefully curated soundscape create the perfect backdrop for a romantic date, a stylish night out, or a late-night gathering with friends. Whether you’re savoring Junmai Daiginjo saké in a private corner booth or dancing under the stars to a live vinyl DJ set, Miru delivers a transportive rooftop dining and nightlife experience—unmistakably New York, with a Tokyo soul.

name: Lalyn
summary: Lalyn is a modern Thai restaurant in Manhattan's Garment District that's known for authentic Thai food with a refined touch and Thai-inspired cocktails, wine and craft beverages.
summary2: Lalyn is a modern Thai restaurant in Manhattan's Garment District, near Midtown, Times Square, and Herald Square. Known for authentic Thai food with a refined touch, Lalyn offers classic dishes like Pad Thai, curries, and fried rice alongside regional specialties, all made with premium ingredients, house-made curry pastes and fresh Thai herbs. Enjoy Thai-inspired cocktails, wine and craft beverages with flavors like lemongrass, pandan and kaffir lime. With a calm, upscale, spa-like atmosphere, Lalyn is ideal for lunch, dinner, date nights, group dining and private events—bringing elevated Thai dining and genuine Thai hospitality to Manhattan.

name: Benihana
summary: Benihana is a dining experience unlike any other: guests are seated at communal tables in groups, where a personal chef will perform the ancient art of teppanyaki.
summary2: Benihana is a dining experience unlike any other: guests are seated at communal tables in groups, where a personal chef will perform the ancient art of teppanyaki. Watch as they slice and dice, preparing a meal of mouth-watering steak, tender chicken or succulent seafood that will dazzle the eyes as well as the taste buds. Also enjoy sushi prepared by a talented sushi chef, and indulge in a specialty cocktail. The restaurant includes a full bar with sushi lounge, great for after-work drinks and meeting friends. Celebrate a special occasion in the elegant private dining rooms.

name: SaiTong Thai
summary: SaiTong, an upscale Thai restaurant located in the Theatre District in Midtown Manhattan, offers an authentic modern Thai dining experience in an elegant, wood-accented atmosphere
summary2: SaiTong is an upscale Thai restaurant located in the Theatre District in Midtown Manhattan, just steps from Times Square. They offer an authentic modern Thai dining experience in an elegant, wood-accented atmosphere, perfect for a romantic night out or after a Broadway show. The restaurant blends the bold flavors of Thailand with a fresh, modern twist. They serve a wide range of contemporary Thai dishes that bring a creative flair to traditional ingredients, while also offering the classic favorites that everyone knows and loves. They also have Thai inspired cocktails and a cozy bar for guests who are just looking for a quick drink.

summary: Located on Manhattan's Upper East Side, Caravaggio boasts elegant Italian cuisine with a modern twist.
summary2: Located on Manhattan's Upper East Side, Caravaggio boasts elegant Italian cuisine with a modern twist. Its sophisticated cooking, flawless service and exquisite modern setting places it among the top restaurants in the City. Giuseppe Bruno—part of the family behind Italian eatery Sistina—launched this latest venture to carry on the family’s tradition of serving great food to devoted patrons.

name: Anassa Taverna - Downtown
summary: Nestled in Battery Park City, Anassa is an elegant interpretation of the traditional Greek taverna.
summary2: Anassa is an elegant interpretation of the traditional Greek taverna. Nestled in Battery Park City, Anassa transports diners through a true culinary and cultural journey through the cobblestone roads of the ancient historical neighborhood of Plaka, featuring simply prepared fresh fish and traditional Greek fare. Within you will find breathtaking decor: a marble-covered bar, light wood furniture and floors, and walls adorned with framed Greek-themed posters and portraits.

name: Quality Meats
summary: A property of the venerable Smith & Wollensky steakhouse overlords, this stylish restaurant is the domain of chef Craig Koketsu and the storied meats of purveyors Milton Abeles and Strassburger Meats.
summary2: A property of the venerable Smith & Wollensky steakhouse overlords, this stylish restaurant is the domain of chef Craig Koketsu and the storied meats of purveyors Milton Abeles and Strassburger Meats. And immediately you'll note what a difference the cut makes. The familiar-sounding menu is anything but—with a keenly focused eye on nouveau American cuisine, Koketsu creates fresh interpretations on everything from seared three filets to roasted chicken with pomegranate to roasted bone marrow. This is all in addition to a spectacular array of seafood.

name: Hanaya Omakase
summary: Chef Yousi Chen serves a 13-course Omakase at his Chef's Counter with an à la carte menu as well.
summary2: Hanaya is chef Yousi Chen's newest venture. After years of experience with sushi legends such as Chef Nakazawa and Chef Nakajima, Chef Yousi has brought an approachable Omakase option to the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood of Manhattan. Chef Yousi serves a 12-course Omakase at his Chef's Counter with an à la carte menu as well. With ingredients sourced from Toyosu Market, the omakase offered at Hanaya offers the season's best ingredients in a carefully curated tasting course. Start with fresh, seasonal bites that lead into an elevated nigiri selection. Chef Yousi has his fish flown in multiple times a week to ensure outstanding quality. Hanaya is open for service from Tuesday through Sunday.

name: Chatti by Regi Mathew
summary: Chatti by Regi Mathew is New York City's first restaurant entirely dedicated to the toddy shops of Kerala, India.
summary2: Chatti by Regi Mathew is New York City's first restaurant entirely dedicated to the toddy shops of Kerala, India. Chef Regi Mathew, one of India's most celebrated chefs, brings a deep connection to Kerala's culinary heritage, combining meticulous research with award-winning expertise to present the rich and vibrant flavors of his home state. From the seafood-rich backwaters of Alleppey to the hearty meat specialties of the Malabar and High Range regions, both the food and drink menus reflect the many flavors of Kerala and the communal spirit of toddy shop dining. Guests have the option to dine in an expansive dining room, take a seat at the full-service bar, or enter the mezzanine level for private dining. Walk-ins are welcome and reservations can be made via OpenTable.
